claim: Masud et al. use attack success probability (ASP) as an attacker-side effectiveness metric
quote: This metric relates to the probability that attacks will be successful.

claim: Masud et al. is a recent MTD evaluation that describes its attacker by the Cyber Kill Chain or ATT&CK
quote: Attackers were modeled after techniques in the cyber kill chain and MITRE ATT&CK, mirroring real threats (Hutchins et al., 2011).
issue: Published 2025 (Computers & Security 153, 104380). Provenance from-memory, but the claim holds.

claim: Masud et al. scored: 1 in part, 2-8 none (Table 3.3)
quote: The attacker’s objective is to breach the database (DB) on host8, which stores critical IoT data. ... 𝐴𝑃 = all_simple_paths (𝐺 , 𝑆𝑠, 𝑇𝑟)
locator: p. 5 printed (PDF p. 5), Sec. 3.1; p. 9 printed (PDF p. 9), Algorithm 2
issue: Marks hold against the model (all simple paths to one target, recomputed per interval, no attacker choice). Adversarial point: the paper's own words 'Vulnerabilities were prioritized by return on attack' (p. 7) could be argued as cost-benefit 'assumed', as Kim's assumed evasion earns 5 in part; the asymmetry is defensible (Kim's script takes the step, Masud's model takes none) and U0279 discloses it.

claim: Masud et al. use an analytical model to evaluate an MTD combining shuffle, diversity and redundancy on an IoT cloud network
quote: (THARM) structures the system into three analytical layers ... we examine the consequences of implementing the shuffle technique in the IoT cloud network.
locator: p. 7 printed (PDF p. 7), Sec. 3.4; p. 10 printed (PDF p. 10), Sec. 3.6.2
issue: The paper also calls its evaluation 'a controlled experiment' on a virtualised host network (p. 7), but the metrics are computed by THARM, a graphical security model; 'analytical model' is fair.

claim: The attacker model is the set of attack paths through a graph model of the network, from the Internet to a target database
quote: attack path possible for attackers from the entrance point (the Internet) to the final target (the database)
issue: Uncited neighbour leaning on masud2025; Algorithm 2 line 6 (all_simple_paths) carries 'the set of attack paths'.

claim: At each deployment interval the model computes each attack path's success probability, cost and RoA, before and after the MTD deploys
quote: Key metrics like attack success probability, attack cost, and attack risk were automatically calculated at intervals using the threat and harm assessment risk model (THARM).
issue: Uncited neighbour; per-path RoA is in Algorithm 2 (lines 7-17, p. 9).

claim: Campaign persistence in part: each attack path is a multi-stage chain of exploits, but paths are computed afresh each interval
quote: We model these network dynamics over time at different points𝑡𝑖 with𝐴𝐺𝑡𝑖 and calculate every possible path of attack at each 𝑡𝑖.

claim: No choice of attack strategy: it has every attack path to the database but chooses none
issue: Uncited neighbour; the p. 7 narrative of 'widespread and focused attacks aiming to breach many or specific high-value hosts' is not reflected in the model and is not mentioned in the dissertation.

claim: No adaptivity: attack paths are recomputed after each deployment, but no next technique is chosen from them
quote: We model these network dynamics over time at different points𝑡𝑖 with𝐴𝐺𝑡𝑖 and calculate every possible path of attack at each 𝑡𝑖.
issue: Uncited neighbour; the paper's 'adaptation to new flaws' (p. 7) is disclosed in U0279.

claim: No cost-benefit reasoning: it computes each path's cost and RoA, but no choice depends on them
quote: RoA is the ratio between how much an attack costs and the benefit it provides. A higher RoA number means that attackers are more likely to take advantage of weaknesses
issue: Uncited neighbour; in Algorithm 3 the computed metrics feed the defender's VM selection, not an attacker choice.

claim: The paper says its attackers prioritise vulnerabilities by RoA and adapt to new flaws (p. 7), but no step of the analytical model does either
quote: Vulnerabilities were prioritized by return on attack, emphasizing those with greatest impact. ... Service and operating system diversification modified configurations, forcing fresh scans and adaptation to new flaws.
issue: Pinpoint exact. Source is passive ('were prioritized'), so 'its attackers' supplies the agent, a fair reading beside Sec. 3.5.4; Algorithms 2-3 contain no attacker selection step.

claim: No objective-specific behaviour: every attack path leads to one objective, the database
quote: The attacker’s objective is to breach the database (DB) on host8, which stores critical IoT data.

claim: No detection avoidance: the analytical model has no IDS for an attack path to avoid
quote: A cyber resilience system supported by an intrusion defence system (IDS) is made more secure with MTD.
issue: Uncited neighbour; the IDS appears only in this general framing, never in THARM or the algorithms (absence from silence).

claim: No learning: each interval's attack paths are computed afresh, nothing from earlier deployments kept
quote: We model these network dynamics over time at different points𝑡𝑖 with𝐴𝐺𝑡𝑖 and calculate every possible path of attack at each 𝑡𝑖.

claim: No deployment-strategy awareness: nothing in the model uses which mechanism deploys next or when
issue: Uncited neighbour; absence claim, consistent with Algorithms 2-3.

claim: Masud et al.'s attacker model has none of the eight properties in full
issue: Uncited summary naming Masud; covered by U0262. Masud's share only checked here.

claim: Masud et al. scored: 1 in part, 2-8 none (Table 6.1)
quote: The attacker’s objective is to breach the database (DB) on host8, which stores critical IoT data. ... 𝐴𝑃 = all_simple_paths (𝐺 , 𝑆𝑠, 𝑇𝑟)
locator: p. 5 printed (PDF p. 5), Sec. 3.1; p. 9 printed (PDF p. 9), Algorithm 2
